entries.change: --memory-swap 16g -> 12g (equal to --memory, so the container gets no swap at all)
entries.reason: The 29 GB of safetensors stream through the container's own page cache, so the cgroup runs flat against memory.max and reclaims 2,000-16,000 times per start. With a 4 GiB swap allowance it spent the allowance to the byte, pushing 3.94 GiB of its own anonymous pages -- including the host staging buffers the card's copy engine reads -- out during the weight load; that is the leading explanation for the bcs copy-engine faults at weight load. With no allowance the same reclaim drops clean, re-readable file pages instead. Validated on three service starts (container pswpout 0, oom_kill 0, 12/12 exact, no fault lines, weight load no slower): experiments/qwen38-27b-b70/notes/2026-09-19-container-memory-cap-swap.md
entries.retire_by: python3 experiments/qwen38-27b-b70/scripts/run-fp8-tp2-acceptance-session.py (fresh depth-5 server on the new launcher), then collect-fp8-tp2-acceptance-evidence.py --raw <session> --out experiments/qwen38-27b-b70/data/2026-09-2x-fp8-two-card-noswap, and repoint DEFAULT at the new packet
